{{Short description|Graded lie algebra structure}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''algebraic bracket''' or '''Nijenhuis–Richardson bracket''' is a [[graded Lie algebra]] structure on the space of [[exterior product|alternating multilinear forms]] of a [[vector space]] to itself, introduced by  [[A. Nijenhuis]] and  [[R. W. Richardson, Jr]] (1966, 1967). It is related to but not the same as the [[Frölicher–Nijenhuis bracket]] and the [[Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket]].

==Definition==
The primary motivation for introducing the bracket was to develop a uniform framework for discussing all possible [[Lie algebra]] structures on a vector space, and subsequently the [[deformation theory|deformations]] of these structures.  If ''V'' is a vector space and {{nowrap|''p'' ≥ −1}} is an integer, let 
:<math>\operatorname{Alt}^p(V) = ({\bigwedge}^{p+1} V^*)\otimes V</math>
be the space of all skew-symmetric {{nowrap|(''p'' + 1)}}-multilinear mappings of ''V'' to itself.  The direct sum Alt(''V'') is a [[graded vector space]].  A '''Lie algebra''' structure on ''V'' is determined by a skew-symmetric bilinear map {{nowrap|''μ'' : ''V'' × ''V'' → ''V''}}.  That is to say, ''μ'' is an element of Alt<sup>1</sup>(''V'').  Furthermore, ''μ'' must obey the [[Jacobi identity]].  The  Nijenhuis–Richardson bracket supplies a systematic manner for expressing this identity in the form {{nowrap|1=[''μ'', ''μ''] = 0}}.

In detail, the bracket is a bilinear bracket operation defined on Alt(''V'') as follows.  On homogeneous elements {{nowrap|''P'' ∈ Alt<sup>''p''</sup>(''V'')}} and {{nowrap|''Q'' ∈ Alt<sup>''q''</sup>(''V'')}}, the Nijenhuis–Richardson  bracket {{nowrap|[''P'', ''Q'']<sup>∧</sup> ∈ Alt<sup>''p''+''q''</sup>(''V'')}} is given by
:<math>[P,Q]^\land = i_P Q - (-1)^{pq}i_Q P .</math>
Here the [[interior product]] ''i''<sub>''P''</sub>  is defined by
:<math>(i_P Q)(X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_{p+q}) = \sum_{\sigma\in \text{Sh}_{q+1,p}}\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma) P(Q(X_{\sigma(0)},X_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,X_{\sigma(q)}),X_{{\sigma(q+1)}},\ldots,X_{{\sigma(p+q)}})</math>
where <math>\text{Sh}_{q+1,p} </math> denotes [[(p,q) shuffle|(''q+1'', ''p'')-shuffle]]s of the indices, i.e. permutations <math>\sigma</math> of <math>\{0,\ldots,p+q\}</math> such that <math>\sigma(0) < \cdots < \sigma(q)</math> and <math>\sigma(q+1) < \cdots < \sigma(p+q)</math>.

On non-homogeneous elements, the bracket is extended by bilinearity.

==Derivations of the ring of forms==
The Nijenhuis–Richardson bracket can be defined on the vector valued forms Ω<sup>*</sup>(''M'', ''T''(''M'')) on a smooth manifold ''M''
in a similar way. Vector valued forms act as derivations on the supercommutative ring Ω<sup>*</sup>(''M'') of forms on ''M''
by taking ''K'' to the derivation ''i<sub>K</sub>'', and the Nijenhuis–Richardson bracket then corresponds to the commutator of two derivations. This identifies Ω<sup>*</sup>(''M'', ''T''(''M'')) with the algebra of derivations that vanish on smooth functions. Not all derivations are of this form; for the structure of the full ring of all derivations see the article [[Frölicher–Nijenhuis bracket]].

The Nijenhuis–Richardson bracket and the Frölicher–Nijenhuis bracket both make Ω<sup>*</sup>(''M'', ''T''(''M'')) into a graded superalgebra, but have different degrees.
